title: Choose the scoreboard's world
question: The roll dealt the Lifeguard Tower Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Lifeguard Tower Board
options.lineage: hand-painted beach tournament scoreboards on lifeguard towers
options.thesis: The score lives on a painted beach board where wooden number cards drop onto hooks.
materials: hanging numeral cards on rope hooks
options.viewport: A red header plank with the countdown as four hanging cards, and four team planks below, each with its animal and two big number cards.
options.risk: Can read as a beach-volleyball cliché if the paint, rope, and card weight are rendered timidly.

raised.raise: Every digit hangs in a fixed slot, so the layout never moves; only cards turn.
A changed card keeps a chalk afterglow for one beat before it settles.
Each team plank carries a chalk tag of its last change, like "+3 LEGO".
Motion is one heavy drop: a card falls with weight and settles, never slides.

options.label: Variety Show Supers
options.thesis: The scoreboard is a variety show's caption layer: bubbly outlined numbers, starbursts, and "+10!!" sound-effect supers.
options.viewport: The timer in a central starburst with four tilted bubble cards around it and a crown on the leader.
options.risk: The familiar choice for a game show, and its noise can fight back-row legibility.

options.label: Boardwalk LED Board
options.thesis: Scores and countdown as lit segments in fixed cells, with unlit ghost segments drawn too.
options.viewport: A segment countdown across the top and four fixed cells of two-digit scores.
options.case: Holds clarity, the most legible scores on the table; loses audience identification, as it has no island or show warmth.
options.risk: Dark grounds wash out on ballroom projectors.

options.label: Struck Cathode
options.thesis: Every value hangs as a ghost; the live one is struck forward in orange.
options.case: Loses both axes: cold lab glow, no show or island.
options.risk: Dark and moody for a tropical charity night.
options.kept: The decay beat: a new value lands while the old one fades over one beat.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Stalls trade shadows, each tagged with its origin.
options.viewport: Four stalls down a moonlit lane.
options.case: Loses both axes: poetic, not a scoreboard.
options.kept: The story stays attached: each item carries a ticket of where it came from.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: Color lives only at the edge; the field stays white.
options.viewport: Quiet white field, pastel fringed cards.
options.case: Loses both axes: too quiet for a game show.
options.kept: Color does a job or stays off the field.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: Pixel numerals towering over the board.
options.case: Loses both axes: design-school register, not the CSA audience's.
options.risk: Reads as a type nerd's poster.
options.kept: One form repeated at several sizes as the whole system.

options.label: Linocut Broadside
options.thesis: Monumental gouged figures and carved demand lettering.
options.viewport: A gouged figure filling the sheet.
options.case: Loses both axes: protest register clashes with a playful charity show.
options.kept: Motion as a single heavy press impression.

canonCard.label: The game-show standard
canonCard.thesis: A glossy TV game-show scoreboard: gradient stage, four glowing panels, a big timer.
canonCard.viewport: Title, centred timer, four equal panels with the leader outlined in gold.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any game-night template by design.
